name: BasicContext
doc: This is a standard context defined by the General Decimal Arithmetic Specification. Precision is set to nine. Rounding is set to ROUND_HALF_UP. All flags are cleared. All traps are enabled (treated as exceptions) except Inexact, Rounded, and Subnormal.

name: Clamped
doc: Altered an exponent to fit representation constraints.

name: Context
signatures: Context(prec=None, rounding=None, Emin=None, Emax=None, capitals=None, clamp=None, flags=None, traps=None)
doc:
Create context.

The context affects almost all operations and controls rounding,
Over/Underflow, raising of exceptions and much more.  A new context
can be constructed as follows:

    >>> c = Context(prec=28, Emin=-425000000, Emax=425000000,
    ...             rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN, capitals=1, clamp=1,
    ...             traps=[InvalidOperation, DivisionByZero, Overflow],
    ...             flags=[])
    >>>

name: abs
doc: Return the absolute value of x.

name: add
doc: Return the sum of x and y.

name: canonical
doc: Return a new instance of x.

name: capitals
doc: Either 0 or 1 (the default). If set to 1, exponents are printed with a capital E; otherwise, a lowercase e is used: Decimal('6.02e+23').

name: clamp
doc: Either 0 (the default) or 1. If set to 1, the exponent e of a Decimal instance representable in this context is strictly limited to the range Emin - prec + 1 <= e <= Emax - prec + 1. If clamp is 0 then a weaker condition holds: the adjusted exponent of the Decimal instance is at most Emax. When clamp is 1, a large normal number will, where possible, have its exponent reduced and a corresponding number of zeros added to its coefficient, in order to fit the exponent constraints; this preserves the value of the number but loses information about significant trailing zeros. For example:

name: clear_flags
doc: Reset all flags to False.

name: clear_traps
doc: Set all traps to False.

name: compare
doc: Compare x and y numerically.

name: compare_signal
doc: Compare x and y numerically.  All NaNs signal.

name: compare_total
doc: Compare x and y using their abstract representation.

name: compare_total_mag
doc: Compare x and y using their abstract representation, ignoring sign.

name: copy
doc: Return a duplicate of the context.

name: copy_abs
doc: Return a copy of x with the sign set to 0.

name: copy_decimal
doc: Return a copy of Decimal x.

name: copy_negate
doc: Return a copy of x with the sign inverted.

name: copy_sign
doc: Copy the sign from y to x.

name: create_decimal
doc:
Create a new Decimal instance from num, using self as the context.

Unlike the Decimal constructor, this function observes the context
limits.

name: create_decimal_from_float
doc:
Create a new Decimal instance from float f.

Unlike the Decimal.from_float() class method, this function observes
the context limits.

name: divide
doc: Return x divided by y.

name: divide_int
doc: Return x divided by y, truncated to an integer.

name: divmod
doc: Return quotient and remainder of the division x / y.

name: Emax
doc: Integers specifying the outer limits allowable for exponents. Emin must be in the range [MIN_EMIN, 0], Emax in the range [0, MAX_EMAX].

name: Emin
doc: Integers specifying the outer limits allowable for exponents. Emin must be in the range [MIN_EMIN, 0], Emax in the range [0, MAX_EMAX].

name: Etiny
doc:
Return a value equal to Emin - prec + 1.

This is the minimum exponent value for subnormal results.  When
underflow occurs, the exponent is set to Etiny.

name: Etop
doc:
Return a value equal to Emax - prec + 1.

This is the maximum exponent if the _clamp field of the context is
set to 1 (IEEE clamp mode).  Etop() must not be negative.

name: exp
doc: Return e ** x.

name: flags
doc: Lists of any signals to be set. Generally, new contexts should only set traps and leave the flags clear.

name: fma
doc: Return x multiplied by y, plus z.

name: is_canonical
doc: Return True if x is canonical, False otherwise.

name: is_finite
doc: Return True if x is finite, False otherwise.

name: is_infinite
doc: Return True if x is infinite, False otherwise.

name: is_nan
doc: Return True if x is a qNaN or sNaN, False otherwise.

name: is_normal
doc: Return True if x is a normal number, False otherwise.

name: is_qnan
doc: Return True if x is a quiet NaN, False otherwise.

name: is_signed
doc: Return True if x is negative, False otherwise.

name: is_snan
doc: Return True if x is a signaling NaN, False otherwise.

name: is_subnormal
doc: Return True if x is subnormal, False otherwise.

name: is_zero
doc: Return True if x is a zero, False otherwise.

name: ln
doc: Return the natural (base e) logarithm of x.

name: log10
doc: Return the base 10 logarithm of x.

name: logb
doc: Return the exponent of the magnitude of the operand's MSD.

name: logical_and
doc:
Applies the logical operation 'and' between each operand's digits.

The operands must be both logical numbers.

    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(Decimal('0'), Decimal('0'))
    Decimal('0')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(Decimal('0'), Decimal('1'))
    Decimal('0')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(Decimal('1'), Decimal('0'))
    Decimal('0')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(Decimal('1'), Decimal('1'))
    Decimal('1')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(Decimal('1100'), Decimal('1010'))
    Decimal('1000')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(Decimal('1111'), Decimal('10'))
    Decimal('10')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(110, 1101)
    Decimal('100')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(Decimal(110), 1101)
    Decimal('100')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_and(110, Decimal(1101))
    Decimal('100')

name: logical_invert
doc:
Invert all the digits in the operand.

The operand must be a logical number.

    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_invert(Decimal('0'))
    Decimal('111111111')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_invert(Decimal('1'))
    Decimal('111111110')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_invert(Decimal('111111111'))
    Decimal('0')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_invert(Decimal('101010101'))
    Decimal('10101010')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_invert(1101)
    Decimal('111110010')

name: logical_or
doc:
Applies the logical operation 'or' between each operand's digits.

The operands must be both logical numbers.

    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(Decimal('0'), Decimal('0'))
    Decimal('0')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(Decimal('0'), Decimal('1'))
    Decimal('1')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(Decimal('1'), Decimal('0'))
    Decimal('1')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(Decimal('1'), Decimal('1'))
    Decimal('1')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(Decimal('1100'), Decimal('1010'))
    Decimal('1110')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(Decimal('1110'), Decimal('10'))
    Decimal('1110')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(110, 1101)
    Decimal('1111')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(Decimal(110), 1101)
    Decimal('1111')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_or(110, Decimal(1101))
    Decimal('1111')

name: logical_xor
doc:
Applies the logical operation 'xor' between each operand's digits.

The operands must be both logical numbers.

    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(Decimal('0'), Decimal('0'))
    Decimal('0')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(Decimal('0'), Decimal('1'))
    Decimal('1')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(Decimal('1'), Decimal('0'))
    Decimal('1')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(Decimal('1'), Decimal('1'))
    Decimal('0')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(Decimal('1100'), Decimal('1010'))
    Decimal('110')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(Decimal('1111'), Decimal('10'))
    Decimal('1101')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(110, 1101)
    Decimal('1011')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(Decimal(110), 1101)
    Decimal('1011')
    >>> ExtendedContext.logical_xor(110, Decimal(1101))
    Decimal('1011')

name: max
doc: Compare the values numerically and return the maximum.

name: max_mag
doc: Compare the values numerically with their sign ignored.

name: min
doc: Compare the values numerically and return the minimum.

name: min_mag
doc: Compare the values numerically with their sign ignored.

name: minus
doc:
Minus corresponds to unary prefix minus in Python.

This operation applies the context to the result.

name: multiply
doc: Return the product of x and y.

name: next_minus
doc: Return the largest representable number smaller than x.

name: next_plus
doc: Return the smallest representable number larger than x.

name: next_toward
doc: Return the number closest to x, in the direction towards y.

name: normalize
doc: Reduce x to its simplest form. Alias for reduce(x).

name: number_class
doc: Return an indication of the class of x.

name: plus
doc:
Plus corresponds to the unary prefix plus operator in Python.

This operation applies the context to the result.

name: power
doc:
Compute a**b.

If 'a' is negative, then 'b' must be integral. The result will be
inexact unless 'a' is integral and the result is finite and can be
expressed exactly in 'precision' digits.  In the Python version the
result is always correctly rounded, in the C version the result is
almost always correctly rounded.

If modulo is given, compute (a**b) % modulo. The following
restrictions hold:

    * all three arguments must be integral
    * 'b' must be nonnegative
    * at least one of 'a' or 'b' must be nonzero
    * modulo must be nonzero and less than 10**prec in absolute
      value

changed.text: The C module computes power() in terms of the correctly rounded exp() and ln() functions. The result is well-defined but only “almost always correctly rounded”.

name: prec
doc: An integer in the range [1, MAX_PREC] that sets the precision for arithmetic operations in the context.

name: quantize
doc: Return a value equal to x (rounded), having the exponent of y.

name: radix
doc: Return 10.

name: remainder
doc:
Return the remainder from integer division.

The sign of the result, if non-zero, is the same as that of the
original dividend.

name: remainder_near
doc:
Return x - y * n.

Here n is the integer nearest the exact value of x / y (if the
result is 0 then its sign will be the sign of x).

name: rotate
doc: Return a copy of x, rotated by y places.

name: rounding
doc: One of the constants listed in the section Rounding Modes.

name: same_quantum
doc: Return True if the two operands have the same exponent.

name: scaleb
doc: Return the first operand after adding the second value to its exp.

name: shift
doc: Return a copy of x, shifted by y places.

name: sqrt
doc: Square root of a non-negative number to context precision.

name: subtract
doc: Return the difference between x and y.

name: to_eng_string
doc: Convert a number to a string, using engineering notation.

name: to_integral_exact
doc: Round to an integer. Signal if the result is rounded or inexact.

name: to_sci_string
doc: Convert a number to a string using scientific notation.

name: traps
doc: Lists of any signals to be set. Generally, new contexts should only set traps and leave the flags clear.

name: Decimal
doc:
Construct a new Decimal object.

value can be an integer, string, tuple, or another Decimal object.  If
no value is given, return Decimal('0'). The context does not affect
the conversion and is only passed to determine if the InvalidOperation
trap is active.

changed.text: The argument to the constructor is now permitted to be a float instance.
Mixed-type comparisons between Decimal instances and other numeric types are now fully supported.
float arguments raise an exception if the FloatOperation trap is set. By default the trap is off.
Underscores are allowed for grouping, as with integral and floating-point literals in code.

name: adjusted
doc: Return the adjusted exponent (exp + digits - 1) of the number.

name: as_integer_ratio
doc:
Return a pair of integers whose ratio is exactly equal to the original.

The ratio is in lowest terms and with a positive denominator.
Raise OverflowError on infinities and a ValueError on NaNs.

name: as_tuple
doc: Return a tuple representation of the number.

name: canonical
doc:
Return the canonical encoding of the argument.

Currently, the encoding of a Decimal instance is always canonical,
so this operation returns its argument unchanged.

name: compare
doc:
Compare self to other.

Return a decimal value:

    a or b is a NaN ==> Decimal('NaN')
    a < b           ==> Decimal('-1')
    a == b          ==> Decimal('0')
    a > b           ==> Decimal('1')

name: compare_signal
doc: Identical to compare, except that all NaNs signal.

name: compare_total
doc:
Compare two operands using their abstract representation.

Similar to the compare() method, but the result gives a total
ordering on Decimal instances.  Two Decimal instances with the same
numeric value but different representations compare unequal in this
ordering:

    >>> Decimal('12.0').compare_total(Decimal('12'))
    Decimal('-1')

Quiet and signaling NaNs are also included in the total ordering.
The result of this function is Decimal('0') if both operands have
the same representation, Decimal('-1') if the first operand is lower
in the total order than the second, and Decimal('1') if the first
operand is higher in the total order than the second operand.  See
the specification for details of the total order.

This operation is unaffected by context and is quiet: no flags are
changed and no rounding is performed.  As an exception, the C
version may raise InvalidOperation if the second operand cannot be
converted exactly.

name: compare_total_mag
doc:
As compare_total(), but ignores the sign of each operand.

x.compare_total_mag(y) is equivalent to
x.copy_abs().compare_total(y.copy_abs()).

This operation is unaffected by context and is quiet: no flags are
changed and no rounding is performed. As an exception, the C version
may raise InvalidOperation if the second operand cannot be converted
exactly.

name: conjugate
doc: Return self.

name: copy_abs
doc:
Return the absolute value of the argument.

This operation is unaffected by context and is quiet: no flags are
changed and no rounding is performed.

name: copy_negate
doc:
Return the negation of the argument.

This operation is unaffected by context and is quiet: no flags are
changed and no rounding is performed.

name: copy_sign
doc:
Return a copy of *self* with the sign of *other*.

For example:

    >>> Decimal('2.3').copy_sign(Decimal('-1.5'))
    Decimal('-2.3')

This operation is unaffected by context and is quiet: no flags are
changed and no rounding is performed. As an exception, the C version
may raise InvalidOperation if the second operand cannot be converted
exactly.

name: exp
doc:
Return the value of the (natural) exponential function e**x.

The function always uses the ROUND_HALF_EVEN mode and the result is
correctly rounded.

name: fma
doc:
Fused multiply-add.

Return self*other+third with no rounding of the intermediate product
self*other.

    >>> Decimal(2).fma(3, 5)
    Decimal('11')

name: from_float
doc: Alternative constructor that only accepts instances of float or int.

name: from_number
doc: Alternative constructor that only accepts instances of float, int or Decimal, but not strings or tuples.

name: is_canonical
doc:
Return True if the argument is canonical and False otherwise.

Currently, a Decimal instance is always canonical, so this operation
always returns True.

name: is_finite
doc: Return True if the argument is a finite number, and False otherwise.

name: is_infinite
doc: Return True if the argument is infinite, and False otherwise.

name: is_nan
doc: Return True if the argument is a (quiet or signaling) NaN, else False.

name: is_normal
doc:
Return True if the argument is a normal number and False otherwise.

Normal number is a finite nonzero number, which is not subnormal.

name: is_qnan
doc: Return True if the argument is a quiet NaN, and False otherwise.

name: is_signed
doc:
Return True if the argument has a negative sign and False otherwise.

Note that both zeros and NaNs can carry signs.

name: is_snan
doc: Return True if the argument is a signaling NaN and False otherwise.

name: is_subnormal
doc:
Return True if the argument is subnormal, and False otherwise.

A number is subnormal if it is non-zero, finite, and has an adjusted
exponent less than Emin.

name: is_zero
doc: Return True if the argument is a zero and False otherwise.

name: ln
doc:
Return the natural (base e) logarithm of the operand.

The function always uses the ROUND_HALF_EVEN mode and the result is
correctly rounded.

name: log10
doc:
Return the base ten logarithm of the operand.

The function always uses the ROUND_HALF_EVEN mode and the result is
correctly rounded.

name: logb
doc:
Return the adjusted exponent of the operand as a Decimal instance.

If the operand is a zero, then Decimal('-Infinity') is returned and
the DivisionByZero condition is raised.  If the operand is an
infinity then Decimal('Infinity') is returned.

name: logical_and
doc:
Applies an 'and' operation between self and other's digits.

Both self and other must be logical numbers.

name: logical_invert
doc:
Invert all its digits.

The self must be logical number.

name: logical_or
doc:
Applies an 'or' operation between self and other's digits.

Both self and other must be logical numbers.

name: logical_xor
doc:
Applies an 'xor' operation between self and other's digits.

Both self and other must be logical numbers.

name: max
doc:
Maximum of self and other.

If one operand is a quiet NaN and the other is numeric, the numeric
operand is returned.

name: max_mag
doc: As the max() method, but compares the absolute values of the operands.

name: min
doc:
Minimum of self and other.

If one operand is a quiet NaN and the other is numeric, the numeric
operand is returned.

name: min_mag
doc: As the min() method, but compares the absolute values of the operands.

name: next_minus
doc: Returns the largest representable number smaller than itself.

name: next_plus
doc: Returns the smallest representable number larger than itself.

name: next_toward
doc:
Returns the number closest to self, in the direction towards other.

If the two operands are unequal, return the number closest to the
first operand in the direction of the second operand.  If both
operands are numerically equal, return a copy of the first operand
with the sign set to be the same as the sign of the second operand.

name: normalize
doc:
Normalize the number by stripping trailing 0s

This also change anything equal to 0 to 0e0.  Used for producing
canonical values for members of an equivalence class.  For example,
Decimal('32.100') and Decimal('0.321000e+2') both normalize to
the equivalent value Decimal('32.1').

name: number_class
doc:
Return a string describing the class of the operand.

The returned value is one of the following ten strings:

    * '-Infinity', indicating that the operand is negative infinity.
    * '-Normal', indicating that the operand is a negative normal
      number.
    * '-Subnormal', indicating that the operand is negative and
      subnormal.
    * '-Zero', indicating that the operand is a negative zero.
    * '+Zero', indicating that the operand is a positive zero.
    * '+Subnormal', indicating that the operand is positive and
      subnormal.
    * '+Normal', indicating that the operand is a positive normal
      number.
    * '+Infinity', indicating that the operand is positive infinity.
    * 'NaN', indicating that the operand is a quiet NaN (Not a
      Number).
    * 'sNaN', indicating that the operand is a signaling NaN.

name: quantize
doc:
Quantize *self* so its exponent is the same as that of *exp*.

Return a value equal to *self* after rounding, with the exponent
of *exp*.

    >>> Decimal('1.41421356').quantize(Decimal('1.000'))
    Decimal('1.414')

Unlike other operations, if the length of the coefficient after the
quantize operation would be greater than precision, then an
InvalidOperation is signaled.  This guarantees that, unless there
is an error condition, the quantized exponent is always equal to
that of the right-hand operand.

Also unlike other operations, quantize never signals Underflow, even
if the result is subnormal and inexact.

If the exponent of the second operand is larger than that of the
first, then rounding may be necessary.  In this case, the rounding
mode is determined by the rounding argument if given, else by the
given context argument; if neither argument is given, the rounding
mode of the current thread's context is used.

name: radix
doc:
Return Decimal(10).

This is the radix (base) in which the Decimal class does all its
arithmetic. Included for compatibility with the specification.

name: remainder_near
doc:
Return the remainder from dividing self by other.

This differs from self % other in that the sign of the remainder is
chosen so as to minimize its absolute value. More precisely, the
return value is self - n * other where n is the integer nearest to
the exact value of self / other, and if two integers are equally
near then the even one is chosen.

If the result is zero then its sign will be the sign of self.

name: rotate
doc:
Returns a rotated copy of self's digits, value-of-other times.

The second operand must be an integer in the range -precision
through precision.  The absolute value of the second operand gives
the number of places to rotate.  If the second operand is positive
then rotation is to the left; otherwise rotation is to the right.
The coefficient of the first operand is padded on the left with
zeros to length precision if necessary.  The sign and exponent of
the first operand are unchanged.

name: same_quantum
doc:
Test whether self and other have the same exponent or both are NaN.

This operation is unaffected by context and is quiet: no flags are
changed and no rounding is performed. As an exception, the C version
may raise InvalidOperation if the second operand cannot be converted
exactly.

name: scaleb
doc:
Return the first operand with the exponent adjusted the second.

Equivalently, return the first operand multiplied by 10**other. The
second operand must be an integer.

name: shift
doc:
Returns a shifted copy of self's digits, value-of-other times.

The second operand must be an integer in the range -precision
through precision.  The absolute value of the second operand gives
the number of places to shift.  If the second operand is positive,
then the shift is to the left; otherwise the shift is to the right.
Digits shifted into the coefficient are zeros.  The sign and
exponent of the first operand are unchanged.

name: sqrt
doc:
Return the square root of the argument to full precision.

The result is correctly rounded using the ROUND_HALF_EVEN rounding
mode.

name: to_eng_string
doc:
Convert to an engineering-type string.

Engineering notation has an exponent which is a multiple of 3, so
there are up to 3 digits left of the decimal place.  For example,
Decimal('123E+1') is converted to Decimal('1.23E+3').

The value of context.capitals determines whether the exponent sign
is lower or upper case.  Otherwise, the context does not affect the
operation.

name: to_integral
doc:
Identical to the to_integral_value() method.

The to_integral() name has been kept for compatibility with older
versions.

name: to_integral_exact
doc:
Round to the nearest integer.

This method signals Inexact or Rounded as appropriate if rounding
occurs.  The rounding mode is determined by the rounding parameter
if given, else by the given context.  If neither parameter is given,
then the rounding mode of the current default context is used.

name: to_integral_value
doc:
Round to the nearest integer without signaling Inexact or Rounded.

The rounding mode is determined by the rounding parameter if given,
else by the given context. If neither parameter is given, then the
rounding mode of the current default context is used.

name: DecimalException
doc: Base class for other signals and a subclass of ArithmeticError.

name: DefaultContext
doc: This context is used by the Context constructor as a prototype for new contexts. Changing a field (such a precision) has the effect of changing the default for new contexts created by the Context constructor.

name: DivisionByZero
doc: Signals the division of a non-infinite number by zero.

name: ExtendedContext
doc: This is a standard context defined by the General Decimal Arithmetic Specification. Precision is set to nine. Rounding is set to ROUND_HALF_EVEN. All flags are cleared. No traps are enabled (so that exceptions are not raised during computations).

name: FloatOperation
doc: Enable stricter semantics for mixing floats and Decimals.

name: getcontext
doc: Get the current default context.

name: HAVE_CONTEXTVAR
doc: The default value is True. If Python is configured using the --without-decimal-contextvar option, the C version uses a thread-local rather than a coroutine-local context and the value is False. This is slightly faster in some nested context scenarios.

name: HAVE_THREADS
doc: The value is True. Deprecated, because Python now always has threads.

name: IEEEContext
doc:
Return a context, initialized as one of the IEEE interchange formats.

The argument must be a multiple of 32 and less than
IEEE_CONTEXT_MAX_BITS.

name: Inexact
doc: Indicates that rounding occurred and the result is not exact.

name: InvalidOperation
doc: An invalid operation was performed.

name: localcontext
doc:
Return a context manager for a copy of the supplied context.

That will set the default context to a copy of ctx on entry to the
with-statement and restore the previous default context when exiting
the with-statement. If no context is specified, a copy of the current
default context is used.

changed.text: localcontext() now supports setting context attributes through the use of keyword arguments.

name: Overflow
doc: Numerical overflow.

name: ROUND_05UP
doc: Round away from zero if last digit after rounding towards zero would have been 0 or 5; otherwise round towards zero.

name: ROUND_CEILING
doc: Round towards Infinity.

name: ROUND_DOWN
doc: Round towards zero.

name: ROUND_FLOOR
doc: Round towards -Infinity.

name: ROUND_HALF_DOWN
doc: Round to nearest with ties going towards zero.

name: ROUND_HALF_EVEN
doc: Round to nearest with ties going to nearest even integer.

name: ROUND_HALF_UP
doc: Round to nearest with ties going away from zero.

name: ROUND_UP
doc: Round away from zero.

name: Rounded
doc: Rounding occurred though possibly no information was lost.

name: setcontext
doc: Set a new default context.

name: SPEC_VERSION
doc: The highest version of the General Decimal Arithmetic Specification that this implementation complies with. See https://speleotrove.com/decimal/decarith.html for the specification.

name: Subnormal
doc: Exponent was lower than Emin prior to rounding.

name: Underflow
doc: Numerical underflow with result rounded to zero.
